scope: The boards students and industry in India use most, ranked. Impulse's board picker shows these first; the knowledge layer has notes for each.

boards.name: Arduino Uno R3
boards.india: The first board of almost every Indian student; CH340 clones upload exactly like the original.

boards.name: Arduino Nano (ATmega328P)
boards.india: Most Nano clones sold in India ship the old bootloader: Impulse selects ATmega328P (Old Bootloader) by default; switch to ATmega328P if the upload fails.

boards.name: ESP32 DevKit V1 (DOIT, 30-pin)
boards.india: The ESP32 board most Indian sellers ship. Onboard LED on GPIO2; CP2102 or CH340 USB-serial; some boards need BOOT held while connecting.

boards.name: NodeMCU 1.0 (ESP-12E / ESP-12F)
boards.india: The classic Indian IoT board (CP2102 or CH340 'V3' clones, both are this board). Use D-pin names; LED on D4 (GPIO2, active-LOW), a second LED on GPIO16 on some boards. VIN is 5 V from USB.

boards.name: Arduino Mega 2560
boards.india: Common in college projects that need many pins (RAMPS 3D printers, LCD shields, multi-sensor rigs).

boards.name: ESP32 Dev Module (38-pin / generic WROOM)
boards.india: The safe choice for any ESP32-WROOM board; also what ESP32 DevKitC and most unbranded 38-pin boards are.

boards.name: Wemos / LOLIN D1 mini
boards.india: Tiny ESP8266 with stackable shields; LED on D4 (GPIO2, active-LOW); 5 V pin from USB; A0 reads 0–3.3 V through the onboard divider.

boards.name: ESP32-CAM (AI Thinker)
boards.india: No USB: upload through an ESP32-CAM-MB adapter or an FTDI on U0R/U0T with GPIO0 tied to GND, then remove the jumper and reset. Needs a solid 5 V supply.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Pico
boards.india: 3.3 V logic. First upload: hold BOOTSEL while plugging in (a drive appears); afterwards the core resets it by itself. LED on GPIO25.

boards.name: Arduino Pro Mini 5 V / 16 MHz
boards.india: No USB: upload through an FTDI/CH340 USB-to-serial adapter on the 6-pin header (DTR to DTR for auto-reset).

boards.name: ESP32-C3 SuperMini
boards.india: The cheapest Wi-Fi board on Indian marketplaces. Native USB only (no UART chip): enable USB CDC On Boot for Serial; LED on GPIO8 (active-LOW); BOOT on GPIO9. GPIO2 and 8 and 9 are strapping pins.

boards.name: STM32F103C8 Blue Pill
boards.india: Very common in Indian colleges. Upload with an ST-Link V2 clone (SWD: SWDIO, SWCLK, GND, 3.3 V) or through a USB-serial adapter on PA9/PA10 with BOOT0 jumper set to 1. LED on PC13 (active-LOW). Many boards carry CKS32/CS32 clone chips that an ST-Link may refuse; pick 'STM32CubeProgrammer (SWD)' or 'Serial' as the upload method.

boards.name: ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 (S3 Dev Module)
boards.india: Two USB-C ports: UART (CP2102) for the usual serial, and the native USB. Serial prints go where USB CDC On Boot says; Impulse sets it from the port you pick. RGB LED on GPIO48 (GPIO38 on some clones).

boards.name: Arduino Uno R4 WiFi
boards.india: Uno R4 with an ESP32-S3 Wi-Fi module and a 12×8 LED matrix; Wi-Fi uses the WiFiS3 library, not WiFiNINA.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Pico W
boards.india: Pico with Wi-Fi/BLE (CYW43439). The LED hangs off the Wi-Fi chip, so LED_BUILTIN works only through the Pico W board selection; Wi-Fi uses WiFi.h (not WiFiNINA).

boards.name: Arduino Leonardo
boards.india: Native USB: Keyboard/Mouse projects; the serial port disappears for a moment at upload (normal).

boards.name: Wemos D1 R32 (ESP32, Uno form)
boards.india: ESP32 in the Uno shape so shields fit, but it is 3.3 V and the Uno pin numbers map to GPIOs (D13 = GPIO18, A0 = GPIO2); motor shields need 5 V logic adapters.

boards.name: NodeMCU-32S (ESP32)
boards.india: 38-pin ESP32 in the NodeMCU layout; LED on GPIO2.

boards.name: ESP-01 / ESP-01S module
boards.india: Only GPIO0 and GPIO2 (plus TX/RX). Upload through a USB adapter with GPIO0 to GND at reset (programmer adapters have a switch). Needs 3.3 V at 300 mA or more; the Uno's 3.3 V pin is not enough. Often used as a Wi-Fi modem for an Uno over AT commands.

boards.name: Wemos LOLIN32 Lite
boards.india: Cheap ESP32 with a LiPo connector and charger; LED on GPIO22 (active-LOW); no 5 V pin.

boards.name: Arduino Uno R4 Minima
boards.india: 32-bit successor of the Uno R3: 5 V logic, 14-bit ADC, 12-bit DAC on A0, same shield footprint.

boards.name: ESP32-WROVER Module
boards.india: ESP32 with 8 MB PSRAM: GPIO16 and GPIO17 belong to the PSRAM and are not available.

boards.name: Arduino Nano Every
boards.india: Pin-compatible with the Nano but a different chip: Serial1 on pins 0/1, 5 V logic, 48 KB flash.

boards.name: Arduino Micro
boards.india: Same chip as the Leonardo in a small breadboard-friendly form.

boards.name: SparkFun Pro Micro (5 V clone)
boards.india: Clones sold as Pro Micro are programmed as Arduino Leonardo (same chip and pin numbers; the clone has no pin 11/12/13 headers but D14–D16 for SPI).

boards.name: STM32F411CE Black Pill (WeAct)
boards.india: USB-C Black Pill: hold BOOT0, tap NRST, release BOOT0 to enter DFU, then upload over USB (upload method 'STM32CubeProgrammer (DFU)'); or use an ST-Link. LED on PC13 (active-LOW), KEY button on PA0. For Serial over USB pick USB support 'CDC (generic Serial supersede U(S)ART)'.

boards.name: ESP32-C3 DevKitM-1 (C3 Dev Module)
boards.india: RISC-V ESP32 with Wi-Fi + BLE 5; RGB LED on GPIO8; native USB and (on DevKitC) a UART bridge.

boards.name: Wemos / LOLIN D1 mini Pro
boards.india: D1 mini with 16 MB flash and an external antenna connector (move the zero-ohm resistor to use it).

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3
boards.india: Thumb-sized C3 with an external antenna connector and battery pads; no user LED; pins are labelled D0–D10 (use the D constants).

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 / Sense
boards.india: User LED on GPIO21 (active-LOW), 8 MB PSRAM; the Sense add-on carries the OV2640 camera and a mic. Native USB: USB CDC On Boot stays enabled.

boards.name: ST Nucleo-F401RE
boards.india: Common in ST-sponsored college labs. Onboard ST-Link: just plug in and upload (method 'Mass Storage' or 'SWD'); Serial goes through the ST-Link's virtual COM port (PA2/PA3). LED LD2 on PA5, user button on PC13.

boards.name: Arduino Pro Mini 3.3 V / 8 MHz
boards.india: 3.3 V logic for sensors and radios (nRF24L01, LoRa modules); upload with a 3.3 V adapter.

boards.name: ESP32-C6 DevKitC-1 (C6 Dev Module)
boards.india: Wi-Fi 6, BLE 5, Zigbee/Thread (802.15.4). RGB LED on GPIO8; two USB-C ports like the S3 kit.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2
boards.india: RP2350: faster, more RAM; same pinout as the Pico. Needs core 4.0 or later.

boards.name: Arduino Nano 33 IoT
boards.india: 3.3 V only (5 V on a pin damages it); Wi-Fi/BLE through WiFiNINA.

boards.name: Digispark ATtiny85 (USB)
boards.india: Plug the board in only AFTER clicking Upload (the Micronucleus bootloader waits 5 s at power-up). P1 drives the LED; P3 and P4 are the USB pins (P3 has a 1.5 kΩ pull-up). Needs the Digistump driver on Windows.

boards.name: ESP32-S3 SuperMini
boards.india: Tiny S3 with native USB only: USB CDC On Boot must be enabled for Serial; RGB LED on GPIO48; hold BOOT (GPIO0) while plugging in if the port does not appear.

boards.name: LilyGO TTGO T-Display (ESP32)
boards.india: 1.14″ ST7789 TFT on GPIO 19 (MOSI), 18 (SCLK), 5 (CS), 16 (DC), 23 (RST), 4 (backlight); buttons GPIO0 and GPIO35; battery voltage on GPIO34. Use TFT_eSPI with the T-Display setup.

boards.name: Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 (V3)
boards.india: ESP32-S3 with SX1262 LoRa (NSS 8, SCK 9, MOSI 10, MISO 11, RST 12, BUSY 13, DIO1 14) and an OLED on SDA 17 / SCL 18 / RST 21, powered through Vext (GPIO36, active-LOW). LED on GPIO35. Use RadioLib or Heltec's library; 865–867 MHz in India.

boards.name: Bare ATmega328P (Uno bootloader)
boards.india: A chip pulled from an Uno or bought with the Optiboot bootloader: wire a 16 MHz crystal, upload through an Uno used as a serial bridge or a USB-serial adapter.

boards.name: Arduino Nano ESP32
boards.india: ESP32-S3 in the Nano form. Tools › Pin Numbering decides whether 13 means D13 or GPIO13: Impulse reads the setting.

boards.name: Arduino Nano 33 BLE / BLE Sense
boards.india: 3.3 V only. BLE through ArduinoBLE; the Sense carries IMU, mic, environment sensors (Rev2 uses different sensor chips and libraries).

boards.name: ESP32-WROVER-KIT
boards.india: Espressif's camera/LCD dev kit around the WROVER module.

boards.name: Wemos LOLIN32
boards.india: LOLIN32 with battery charger; LED on GPIO5.

boards.name: Wemos D1 Mini ESP32
boards.india: ESP32 in the D1 mini footprint (D1 mini shields fit).

boards.name: Wemos LOLIN D32
boards.india: ESP32 with LiPo charger and battery voltage on GPIO35 (divider /2).

boards.name: ST Nucleo-F446RE
boards.india: Same board shape and pins as the F401RE with a faster F446 (180 MHz).

boards.name: ATtiny85 (ATTinyCore, via ISP)
boards.india: Programmed with an Arduino as ISP or a USBasp: set Tools › Programmer and use Upload Using Programmer. Internal 8 MHz clock by default (Burn Bootloader sets the fuses).

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO RP2040
boards.india: Thumb-sized RP2040; user LED (GPIO25 red, 16 green, 17 blue, active-LOW) and a NeoPixel on GPIO12 powered by GPIO11.

boards.name: Waveshare RP2040-Zero
boards.india: Very cheap RP2040 with a WS2812 LED on GPIO16 and USB-C; hold BOOT while plugging in for the first upload.

boards.name: ESP-12F / ESP-12E bare module
boards.india: The module on a custom PCB: GPIO15 to GND, EN and GPIO0/GPIO2 pulled up (GPIO0 low to flash), 3.3 V only.

boards.name: ESP32-S2 Dev Module (Saola-1)
boards.india: Single-core, Wi-Fi only, native USB (no Bluetooth).

boards.name: Wemos LOLIN S2 Mini
boards.india: Cheap S2 in the D1 mini footprint; LED on GPIO15; BOOT on GPIO0.

boards.name: Wemos LOLIN C3 Mini
boards.india: D1 mini footprint with an ESP32-C3; RGB LED on GPIO7.

boards.name: Wemos LOLIN S3 Mini
boards.india: D1 mini footprint with an ESP32-S3; RGB LED on GPIO47.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
boards.india: Pico 2 with Wi-Fi/BLE; same notes as the Pico W.

boards.name: Teensy 4.0
boards.india: 600 MHz Cortex-M7, 3.3 V and NOT 5 V tolerant. Press the button on the board if the upload does not start (Teensy Loader).

boards.name: Teensy 4.1
boards.india: Teensy 4.0 with more pins, SD slot, Ethernet pads and PSRAM pads.

boards.name: LilyGO TTGO LoRa32 (OLED)
boards.india: SX1276/78 LoRa on SPI (SCK 5, MISO 19, MOSI 27, CS 18, RST 14, DIO0 26) and a 0.96″ SSD1306 OLED on SDA 21 / SCL 22 (V1: SDA 4 / SCL 15, RST 16). India uses 865–867 MHz.

boards.name: Heltec WiFi Kit 32 (V3)
boards.india: ESP32-S3 with an OLED on SDA 17 / SCL 18 / RST 21 (Vext GPIO36 must be LOW to power it); LED on GPIO35.

boards.name: ESP32-C6 SuperMini
boards.india: Native USB only: enable USB CDC On Boot; LED on GPIO8 (varies by seller), BOOT on GPIO9.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C6
boards.india: C6 in the XIAO footprint; antenna switch pins GPIO3 and GPIO14 are used by the board.

boards.name: DFRobot FireBeetle 2 ESP32-E
boards.india: Low-power ESP32 with charger; LED on GPIO2.

boards.name: ESP32-PICO-KIT (PICO-D4)
boards.india: ESP32 system-in-package dev kit.

boards.name: Arduino MKR WiFi 1010
boards.india: 3.3 V MKR form factor; WiFiNINA; LiPo charger onboard.

boards.name: Arduino Nano RP2040 Connect
boards.india: RP2040 with a u-blox Wi-Fi module (WiFiNINA), IMU and mic.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO SAMD21
boards.india: Tiny 3.3 V board; double-tap RESET pads to enter the bootloader if an upload fails.

boards.name: LilyPad Arduino
boards.india: E-textile projects; needs an FTDI adapter to upload.

boards.name: Bare ATmega2560 (Mega bootloader)
boards.india: The chip of the Mega on a custom PCB; programmed like the Mega.

boards.name: ST Nucleo-L476RG
boards.india: Low-power L4 Nucleo used in battery projects; same layout as the F401RE.

boards.name: STM32F407 Discovery (STM32F4DISCOVERY)
boards.india: Four user LEDs (PD12–PD15), accelerometer, audio codec; onboard ST-Link uploads.

boards.name: STM32F401CC Black Pill (WeAct)
boards.india: The cheaper Black Pill (256 KB flash, 64 KB RAM); same upload notes as the F411.

boards.name: M5Stack Core2
boards.india: Touch display, speaker, IMU, AXP192 power chip: use the M5Core2 / M5Unified library, which configures all of it.

boards.name: M5Stack AtomS3
boards.india: Tiny S3 with a 0.85″ screen and IMU; use M5Unified / M5AtomS3.

boards.name: LilyGO T-Display-S3
boards.india: 1.9″ parallel ST7789 display (8-bit bus GPIO39–48 region), buttons GPIO0 and GPIO14; USB native; TFT_eSPI needs the T-Display-S3 setup.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO nRF52840
boards.india: BLE wearables; charger onboard; use the 'Seeed nRF52 Boards' core (not the mbed one) unless a library needs mbed.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO nRF52840 Sense
boards.india: Adds an IMU (LSM6DS3) and a PDM microphone to the XIAO nRF52840.

boards.name: Adafruit Feather ESP32 V2
boards.india: NeoPixel on GPIO0, STEMMA QT connector, I2C power pin.

boards.name: Adafruit ESP32 Feather
boards.india: Imported; Feather pin names (A0–A5 differ from GPIO numbers), battery on A13.

boards.name: Adafruit QT Py ESP32-S3
boards.india: Imported; NeoPixel on GPIO39 with power on GPIO38; STEMMA QT connector.

boards.name: Adafruit Feather RP2040
boards.india: Imported; NeoPixel on GPIO16, LED on GPIO13, STEMMA QT.

boards.name: SparkFun Pro Micro RP2040
boards.india: Pro Micro footprint; WS2812 on GPIO25.

boards.name: Generic RP2040 board
boards.india: Any RP2040 board without its own entry (set the flash size in Board Options).

boards.name: Arduino Due
boards.india: 3.3 V SAM3X; two USB ports (Programming port for uploads).

boards.name: Arduino Zero
boards.india: SAMD21 with an onboard debugger (EDBG port).

boards.name: Arduino MKR Zero
boards.india: SAMD21 with an SD slot and I2S for audio.

boards.name: Arduino MKR1000
boards.india: Older MKR Wi-Fi board (WiFi101 library).

boards.name: Arduino Uno WiFi Rev2
boards.india: Rare in India; WiFiNINA library for the u-blox module.

boards.name: Seeed Studio Wio Terminal
boards.india: SAMD51 with a 2.4″ screen, buttons, Wi-Fi/BLE via RTL8720; used in some school programs.

boards.name: Olimex ESP32-POE
boards.india: Ethernet with Power-over-Ethernet for industrial installs; Ethernet uses the LAN8720 PHY on fixed pins.

boards.name: DFRobot FireBeetle ESP32
boards.india: Earlier FireBeetle; LED on GPIO2.

boards.name: Adafruit Feather HUZZAH ESP8266
boards.india: Imported; LED on GPIO0 (active-LOW) and GPIO2; LiPo charger.

boards.name: NodeMCU 0.9 (ESP-12)
boards.india: The wide first NodeMCU; same pins as 1.0 but it does not fit a breadboard.

boards.name: Wemos D1 R1 (ESP8266, Uno form, old)
boards.india: The first Uno-shaped Wemos; its D-pin mapping differs from the D1 mini, so pick R1 only for the old board.

boards.name: Wemos D1 R2 (ESP8266, Uno form)
boards.india: ESP8266 in the Uno shape; programmed as the D1 mini (same pin mapping, 3.3 V logic).

boards.name: Adafruit Feather nRF52840 Express
boards.india: Imported; Bluefruit library; NeoPixel on pin 8.

boards.name: Nordic nRF52840 DK (PCA10056)
boards.india: Nordic's dev kit, programmed through the Adafruit nRF52 core with its onboard J-Link.

boards.name: ATtiny84 (ATTinyCore, via ISP)
boards.india: 14-pin ATtiny with more I/O; programmed like the ATtiny85.

boards.name: ATtiny1614 (megaTinyCore, UPDI)
boards.india: Modern tinyAVR programmed over one UPDI pin with a cheap USB-serial adapter and a 4.7 kΩ resistor (SerialUPDI). 16 KB flash, 2 KB RAM, 20 MHz.

boards.name: ATtiny1616 (megaTinyCore, UPDI)
boards.india: 20-pin tinyAVR 1-series; same UPDI programming as the ATtiny1614.
